title: EPA throws in the towel on policing air pollution from factory farms
gist: The EPA ended its 20-plus-year effort, begun under the 2005 Air Consent Agreement, to develop methods for estimating air emissions from factory farms, which in effect abandons Clean Air Act regulation of CAFOs just before the midterms. Advocates note that the amnesty also ends, so legal obligations remain and lawsuits could rely on other methods such as California's models.

insights.claim: The EPA announced it will end its 20-plus-year effort to develop methods for monitoring air pollution from factory farms, which effectively shuts down its attempts to regulate CAFOs under the Clean Air Act.
